package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious document, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of Windows and Windows Server with MSDT enabled
package_info.why_malicious: This document exploits the ms-msdt:// URL protocol handler vulnerability (CVE-2022-30190, 'Follina') to trigger the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) from within a Word document. By abusing this mechanism, attackers achieve remote code execution with the privileges of the current user, enabling installation of additional malware, data theft, or creation of new user accounts. This represents a critical security risk due to the ability to execute arbitrary code without user interaction beyond document open or preview.

execution_context.trigger: At document open or preview (import-time in Word)
execution_context.file_location: Word document (remote template reference in document XML, typically in word/_rels/document.xml.rels or main document XML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open or preview, the Word document uses the INCLUDEPICTURE field to fetch an external HTML file from an attacker-controlled server over HTTP, causing Word to retrieve and process remote content, which initiates the next stage of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Word documents should not fetch remote HTML templates from untrusted sources, as this can be used to deliver malicious payloads or trigger exploitation chains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents reference local or trusted internal resources for templates and images, not arbitrary external domains controlled by attackers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Corporate environments may use remote templates or images hosted on internal, trusted servers, but referencing unknown or public internet domains is highly unusual and risky.
key_indicators: INCLUDEPICTURE field referencing external HTTP/HTTPS URL
Remote template or image URL pointing to untrusted or attacker-controlled domain
Word document XML containing external resource references

execution_context.trigger: When the remote HTML file is loaded by Word (runtime in mshtml rendering engine)
execution_context.file_location: payload.html (served by attacker, loaded by Word as remote template)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the remote HTML payload is loaded by Word, the embedded JavaScript executes at runtime and redirects the process to a specially crafted ms-msdt:// URI, causing the operating system to invoke the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool with attacker-controlled parameters, which sets up the next stage of code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTML content loaded in the context of a Word document should not invoke OS-level protocol handlers, especially those capable of launching system diagnostic tools with arbitrary parameters.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate HTML templates used in Office documents do not redirect to ms-msdt:// or similar protocol handlers, nor do they attempt to launch system utilities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Use of protocol handlers from HTML is rare and typically restricted to trusted, internal applications with explicit user consent; it is not expected in Office document workflows.
key_indicators: JavaScript in HTML payload redirecting to ms-msdt:// URI
Redirection to protocol handler from Office context
Presence of ms-msdt:// in HTML or JavaScript loaded by Office

execution_context.trigger: When MSDT is launched via ms-msdt:// protocol (runtime, as a child process of Word or mshtml)
execution_context.file_location: Invoked by ms-msdt:// URI (process context, not a file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ms-msdt:/id PCWDiagnostic /skip force /param ... (parameters include PowerShell command to download and execute payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When MSDT is launched via the ms-msdt:// protocol, attacker-supplied parameters are passed to MSDT, which executes embedded PowerShell code. This PowerShell command downloads and executes additional payloads from the attacker's infrastructure, resulting in arbitrary code execution under the user's privileges.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: MSDT should not be invoked with arbitrary parameters from untrusted sources, especially those that result in execution of PowerShell commands capable of downloading and running further malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Diagnostic tools like MSDT are intended for troubleshooting and should not execute arbitrary code or scripts provided by Office documents or remote HTML.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: MSDT may be legitimately used for system diagnostics, but not with attacker-controlled scripts or parameters originating from Office documents or untrusted HTML.
key_indicators: ms-msdt:// protocol invocation with embedded PowerShell payload
Execution of PowerShell as a child process of msdt.exe or WINWORD.EXE
Suspicious command-line parameters passed to msdt.exe

attack_chain.action: Victim opens or previews a malicious Word document, which contains an INCLUDEPICTURE field referencing a remote HTML template.
attack_chain.leads_to: Word fetches and loads attacker-controlled HTML content.

attack_chain.action: Word loads the remote HTML payload, which executes JavaScript to redirect to the ms-msdt:// protocol handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: MSDT is launched with attacker-supplied parameters via the ms-msdt:// URI.

attack_chain.action: MSDT executes attacker-supplied PowerShell code, resulting in arbitrary code execution (such as malware installation, data theft, or system compromise).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: system compromise, data exfiltration, or further malware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Office process (e.g., WINWORD.EXE) launching msdt.exe as a child process
Office document fetching remote HTML templates or images via INCLUDEPICTURE or remote template fields
ms-msdt:// protocol handler invoked from within Office or mshtml context
PowerShell execution as a child of msdt.exe or WINWORD.EXE
file_indicators: Word documents containing INCLUDEPICTURE fields with external HTTP/HTTPS URLs
Word document XML referencing remote templates or images in word/_rels/document.xml.rels or main document XML
HTML payloads containing ms-msdt:// URIs or JavaScript redirection to protocol handlers
network_indicators: Office applications making HTTP/HTTPS requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains
Connections to attacker infrastructure (e.g., tibet-gov.web.app, coolrat.xyz, or other domains referenced in INCLUDEPICTURE fields or HTML payloads)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Office processes (e.g., WINWORD.EXE) for child processes invoking msdt.exe, especially with suspicious or unexpected command-line parameters. Scan Office documents for INCLUDEPICTURE or remote template fields referencing external domains. Inspect network traffic for Office applications making HTTP/HTTPS requests to untrusted or non-corporate domains. Analyze logs for ms-msdt:// protocol handler invocations originating from Office or mshtml processes. Detect PowerShell execution chains where the parent process is msdt.exe or WINWORD.EXE, and correlate with recent document activity.
